subject: Request: AWS marketplace credit for legacy EdgeBank account

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@edgebank.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@edgebank.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS marketplace credit request for legacy EdgeBank account

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. EdgeBank has been using Redwood in a couple of pilot environments for ~18 months, and we are ready to expand across three production teams — but procurement flagged the marketplace listing pricing for our renewal.

We purchase through the AWS marketplace and the list price leaves us with a material uplift vs. direct contracting. To move forward fast we need either a 25% marketplace credit or an equivalent one-time onboarding credit applied to the first 12 months. This is a retention/velocity ask; we expect to commit to a 36-month usage forecast (see attached deck) if we can resolve pricing.

Attachments: edgebank-procurement-deck.pdf (procurement summary, forecast, and SSO/KMS requirements)

Can you route this to the deal desk and confirm timelines? We need an answer before next Monday to hit our internal purchasing cutover.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Head of Procurement
EdgeBank

Aisha — reviewed the deck and forecast. Quick assessment:

- EdgeBank is borderline for a private offer (their forecast qualifies for a negotiated private offer).
- Marketplace listing prevents us from giving an off-market price directly, but we can:
  * Create a private offer (via AWS) with an upfront credit applied for the first 12 months, or
  * Issue a one-time Redwood credit redeemable against invoices tied to the HubSpot deal (works for hosted customers but is operationally heavier).

Recommendation: pursue an AWS private offer with a marketplace-backed credit. Operationally that keeps billing on the marketplace and avoids changing standard listing pricing. For a long-standing customer with a 36-month outlook, I recommend a 20% credit for 12 months plus waiver of the AWS listing fee for year one. This balances unit economics and retention risk.

Attached: pricing-matrix.xlsx (scenarios: 10%/15%/20% credits; impact to ARR and GP)

Next steps: Rishi — can Deal Desk confirm if 20% + listing-fee waiver is approvable, and if we need exec sign-off?

Thanks,
Marcus
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: AWS marketplace credit request for legacy EdgeBank account

Marcus / Aisha — reviewed the recommendation and the attached matrix. I’m comfortable approving a 20% credit applied to the first 12 months on the AWS private offer, plus a waiver of the listing fee for year one, subject to the following:

1) A signed PO or master purchase agreement referencing Redwood deal RDW-202705-EB-142 and the private-offer ID.
2) Discount capped to 20% for the first 12 months; after that standard marketplace pricing applies unless we renew the concession through normal renewal channels.
3) Finance needs to code the credit as a contra-revenue line and track through HubSpot for reporting.

I’ve attached a brief approval note for Deal Desk records. If legal needs to add contract language for marketplace credits, loop in legal and procurement.

Attachments: dealdesk-approval-note.txt
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/tx/1234-abcd (PO template)

If there are no further objections, I’ll mark this approved so Marcus/Aisha can communicate to EdgeBank and start the private-offer flow with AWS.

— Rishi
